messages:
sophia: Heads up: noticed weird quota diffs during yesterday's v1->v2 canary. Token counts in billing pipeline didn't match runtime logs for a handful of tenants. Suspect session-affinity flips mid-session are double-counting. :thinking_face:

miguel: I saw that too. The canary reduced session-affinity TTL to avoid long sticky sessions, but some clients maintain long-lived websocket sessions and expect consistent routing. When the server rebalances, metrics show the same request id hitting two model variants for a short window.

margo: We should avoid retrofitting customers' billing after a routing change if we can attribute tokens deterministically. Proposal: introduce a migration session id header `X-Redwood-Migration-Session: <uuid>` generated at first request for a logical session. Use that to attribute all tokens from that session to the initial variant for a configurable grace window (default 30s).

devex-charles: Strong +1 for an explicit session header. Also helps SDKs and customers who want deterministic routing. We can add a non-breaking opt-in flow in SDKs to emit the header. Docs should call it out under "Compatibility and Billing" so teams know expectation.

infra-bot: alert: billing-reconcile-warning for tenant: beta-co (route /embed-text)  discrepancy +8% over 6h

sophia: For telemetry I'd rather emit compact boundary events instead of relying solely on request logs. Something like `migration.session_start` and `migration.variant_switch` with minimal fields (tenant, route, session_id, prev_variant, next_variant). That keeps tracing low-cardinality but gives us correlation points.

miguel: And on the billing side: implement a dedupe window where token-attribution checks for a recent session_id and if found, drop duplicates from the new variant's meter and add them to the origin's ledger instead. We must be careful not to lose real duplicates from retries.

margo: To handle retries we can require the presence of both `session_id` and `request_id` and dedupe only when request_id differs but session_id matches and timestamp delta < grace_window. Also log a small `migration.duplicate_deduped` metric for visibility.

devex-charles: Console UX asks: surface a "Migration sessions" mini-timeline per route so customers can see session churn and whether any meter adjustments occurred. Also add a short banner during rollout: "Compatibility mode active: tokens attributed to initial variant for Xs" with a link to a reconciliation FAQ.

infra-bot: deploy: canary v2-routing-config -> infra-canary-2 (commit sha: c3f9a1e)

sophia: Important operational item: add an internal debug endpoint `/internal/debug/migration_session?session_id=` that returns the current variant history for that session. Admin-only. SRE will need it when customers file billing disputes.

miguel: We'll need to coordinate the quota pipeline change carefully. My plan: feature-flag billing dedupe behind `migration.dedupe_v1v2` so we can enable for a subset of tenants and validate ledger parity before wide rollout.

margo: Timeline: I'll mock console timeline this afternoon. Can we aim to have header + telemetry PR by EOD and the feature-flagged billing dedupe in staging next week?

devex-charles: I'll update SDKs to expose an opt-in for emitting `X-Redwood-Migration-Session` and draft the migration FAQ + billing copy. Also suggest a short billing-grade test page in Console so customers can run a synthetic session and see the attribution.

sophia: Good. One more: add an alert mapping so that when `migration.duplicate_deduped` spikes we link directly to the route's migration timeline and the commit that last changed affinity behavior. That will speed triage.

miguel: Agreed. I'll add alert->console-link and a small `migration.session_churn` metric.

margo: ACK. I'll post designs to #design later and tag devex for copy review.

sophia: Thanks all 44d — this should reduce surprise invoices and give customers stronger visibility into compatibility during rollouts.
